summary.headline: Hikal Q2 FY27 revenue INR434 crore, EBITDA margin 10.3%, PAT negative INR6 crore; management reiterates mid-teens revenue growth guidance for FY27.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR434 crore with EBITDA of INR45 crore (10.3% margin) and PAT of negative INR6 crore; H1 revenue was INR837 crore, EBITDA INR82 crore (9.8%) and PAT negative INR14 crore. Margins were hit by raw material and solvent price spikes (some over 100%), Chinese pricing pressure in crop protection, and about INR20 crore annual US FDA remediation cost. Pharma EBIT margin was 4.6% on capacity utilisation of only 60-70%, while Crop Protection was loss-making at EBIT margin of negative 1.5%. Management says H2 will be significantly better than H1 and reiterated full-year guidance of mid-teens revenue growth and substantial profitability improvement.

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR278 crore, EBIT INR13 crore (4.6% margin); H1 revenue INR511 crore, EBIT margin 4%. Utilisation 60-70% due to deliberate slowdown for quality compliance; Swissmedic GMP certificate received for Bangalore; 28 customer audits passed.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR156 crore, EBIT negative INR2 crore (negative 1.5%); H1 revenue INR326 crore, EBIT negative INR8 crore. Legacy portfolio drove volume growth; CDMO demand deferred to H2; new multiyear CDMO contract with a European agrochemical company, launch expected around end FY27.

segments.name: Animal Health and Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Animal Health grew year-on-year with contribution margin up QoQ; target about INR400 crore by FY30; 6 CDMO products under development, 3 new KSMs under validation. Panoli multipurpose facility began commercial production for Specialty Ingredients (UV filters, skin care); no revenue figure given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance reiterated: mid-teens revenue growth and substantial improvement in profitability; H2 expected significantly better than H1 on revenue and EBITDA.

Management expects Pharma EBITDA margin around 18-19% and EBIT margin 12-13% once remediation shutdowns end; with about INR20 crore remediation cost removed, group EBITDA margin could be near 17-18% by end of FY27.
If US FDA reinspection clears, pharma revenue could add about INR150 crore annualised (45-46% contribution), with pending CDMO contracts on top; reinspection hoped for by end of FY27.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin at least equal to last year's H2 (about 18.5%) only if war/Middle East situation normalises; otherwise up to 100 bps lower.
Agrochemical CDMO contract expected to contribute INR50-75 crore per year at peak (around calendar 2029); realistic volumes from next year.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex INR81 crore for debottlenecking, inventory, regulatory upgrades and selective capacity creation.
Panoli multipurpose facility commenced commercial production of Specialty Ingredients this year; focus now on stabilisation and customer validation.
Repurposed Phase I facility from agrochemicals began Personal Care manufacturing a couple of months ago; Phase II repurposing for human and animal health CDMO by end of next year.
Pharma utilisation 60-70% in Q2 due to quality-driven slowdown and plant shutdowns for upgrades to meet US FDA commitments.
Panoli pilot plant built about a year ago; DMF filings from Panoli to be about 4 products this year, rising to 6-7 if Bangalore clears.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices, especially key solvents and some commodities, rose over 100% in some cases; majority of increase in CDMO to be passed on to customers over the next few quarters, and majority of crop price increases being passed on.

Chinese competition kept global crop protection prices under severe pressure; customers buying only for immediate needs. Management says the worst of the crop downcycle is behind, with channel inventory depleting.
Pharma customer traction strengthened in Latin America, Japan and Korea; regulatory approvals in China and Brazil for 2 established products.
Gabapentin share of pharma business is declining; gross margin on Gabapentin about 35% versus pharma overall 45-46%.
Personal Care: small niche product portfolio entering validation, market testing in next couple of months; contract manufacturing is the larger focus.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Pharma Q2 EBIT margin 4.6% versus 13.7% in Q2 FY25 on similar revenue, and what is normalised margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower contribution margin from raw material prices and product mix, plus higher fixed costs from US FDA remediation that were absent in FY25. Analyst's view that normalised pharma EBIT margin should be above 10% was accepted by management.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the new agrochemical CDMO contract and what margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Niche proprietary off-patent active ingredient, worked on for about 3 years; commercial production by end of next quarter; peak revenue around 2029-early 2030 with INR50-75 crore per year; margins well above company average, with backward integration into key starting material and pricing roadmap from customer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue upside from US FDA clearance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR150 crore annualised revenue uplift on a like-for-like basis 12 months after clearance, at 45-46% contribution, excluding pending Bangalore CDMO contracts that convert after reinspection.

qa_highlights.question: What is the annual US FDA remediation cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore annualised, varying quarter to quarter; expected to persist until end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Gabapentin margin and dependence discussed, and is there price erosion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no severe price erosion; raw material increases are largely passed through. Gabapentin is lower margin but a volume driver, and its share is falling as new higher-margin products launch in diabetes, gastro, CNS, cardio, with oncology next.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Bangalore facility become main supplier to customers after clearance?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; the customer currently sources primarily from a European supplier after the warning letter, and management expects Hikal to become main source once FDA reinspection clears.

risks_watch: US FDA reinspection of Bangalore facility timing (hoped by end FY27) and outcome; Bangalore CDMO approvals on hold pending clearance.
Raw material and solvent cost inflation (some over 100%) and speed of price pass-through to CDMO and crop customers.
Middle East war and energy cost impact on margins; H2 margin recovery conditional on normalisation.
Continued Chinese dumping and pricing pressure in crop protection; crop CDMO demand deferred to H2.
Pharma utilisation of only 60-70% and the ~INR20 crore annual remediation cost weighing on fixed-cost absorption.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H2 recovery and the FDA outcome, but cautious on near-term margins, which management attributes to raw material costs and the war situation. Several analyst questions on margin bridges and quantification were answered vaguely or deferred offline (e.g., FY25 fixed-cost comparison).
key_quotes: We reiterate our full year guidance given in the last quarter for a mid-teens growth in revenue and a substantial improvement in profitability.
So this 2025 inspection will be an aberration, and we will never get into this situation again.
Once the re-inspection comes, those CDMO contracts will convert into commercial supply.
It's a high-margin business with a contribution margin well in excess of the contribution margin of the current crop division.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 mid-teens revenue growth (no number-level order book given) and a substantial profitability improvement, backed partly by the US FDA reinspection path (~INR150 crore annualised pharma revenue if cleared, reinspection hoped by end FY27), a CDMO contract launching around end FY27, and price pass-through, while pharma utilisation sits at only 60-70%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides pharma EBITDA margin to 18-19% and group EBITDA near 17-18% by end FY27 once ~INR20 crore remediation cost ends, but Q2 EBITDA margin was only 10.3% and H1 9.8%, and H2 margin recovery is conditional on the Middle East situation normalising (otherwise up to 100 bps lower).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Phase II repurposing by end of next year (FY28)
rows.why: Panoli multipurpose facility is already commissioned for Specialty Ingredients and Phase I repurposing is live for Personal Care, but pharma utilisation is only 60-70%, so no new large capacity is needed near term; Phase II CDMO repurposing is due by end of next year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterates mid-teens FY27 revenue growth and says H2 will be significantly better than H1 (H1 revenue INR837 crore), with CDMO demand deferred into H2 and channel inventory depleting in crop protection, though no order-book figures were given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Q2 capex was INR81 crore for debottlenecking and regulatory upgrades, and utilisation is only 65%, so a large new capex announcement is not needed, though a capex plan tied to FDA clearance or CDMO contracts could emerge.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held guidance at mid-teens revenue growth and substantial profitability improvement, but H1 EBITDA margin was 9.8% and PAT was negative INR14 crore, so an upgrade looks unlikely in the window.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 recovery is conditional on war/Middle East normalisation and US FDA reinspection (hoped by end FY27), with raw material and solvent prices up over 100% in some cases and crop pricing pressured by Chinese competition.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Personal Care products are already being manufactured and enter validation/market testing in the next couple of months; DMF filings from Panoli are about 4 products this year, and the agro CDMO contract launches around end FY27 with commercial production by end of next quarter.

rows.label: New agrochemical CDMO contract ramp
rows.why: Multiyear European contract expected to add INR50-75 crore per year at peak (around calendar 2029), with realistic volumes from next year and margins well above company average.

rows.label: US FDA Bangalore reinspection and clearance
rows.why: If reinspection clears, pharma revenue could add about INR150 crore annualised at 45-46% contribution, plus pending Bangalore CDMO contracts, but timing and outcome are uncertain.

rows.label: Remediation cost roll-off
rows.why: About INR20 crore annual US FDA remediation cost is expected to persist until end FY27, after which removing it supports the margin recovery to 17-18% group EBITDA.
